Subject: Expanding to additional projects — timing & terms question

Hi Jasmine,

Quick one — the engineering org at Asteria just approved two more product teams that want to start production on Redwood next quarter (roughly 6 new projects total). We have the renewal coming up in mid-December for our current committed capacity. Before we lock the renewal, procurement asked whether adding these extra projects can be folded into the same commitment window (we'd prefer a single PO) and if there are discounted increments for the additional capacity.

High level: +6 projects, need API keys and onboarding for each project, target rollout across 3 weeks in Jan. Can you share the options (pricing delta, term extensions, and API key provisioning timeline)? Also looping in procurement separately on next steps.

Thanks,
Ari
Ari Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering | Asteria Labs
ari@asterialabs.com

Hi Ari — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the approvals. This is something we can definitely accommodate without forcing multiple POs; below is a proposed approach and immediate asks so we can align before your renewal deadline.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Fold the 6 new projects into the existing account under the next renewal PO. We’ll support additional API keys per project and tiered capacity buckets.
- Pricing options: short-term add-on (month-to-month for Q1) vs. commit adjustment (12‑month uplift with stepped discount). Ben’s included on this thread for precise terms.
- Rollout ops: Laura will own key provisioning + onboarding checklist. Typical delivery: API keys + sandbox access in 2 business days per project after kickoff; production keys after completed smoke tests (1–2 days).

Immediate asks from Asteria so we can finalize the quote by Wed (2026-12-02):
1) Confirm whether you want the add-ons billed into the current renewal PO or as a separate short-term addendum.
2) Provide target concurrency per new project (avg tokens/sec or QPS) so we can size burst vs reserved capacity.
3) Any internal compliance requirements (SOC2 evidence or IP whitelisting) beyond what we already have on file.

I’ve attached a draft MA amendment that shows two pricing paths — month-to-month add-on vs. committed uplift with a discount schedule. Ben — can you review and flag the best fit for Asteria? Laura — I’ll defer rollout sequencing to you for timing.

Thanks — Jasmine

Thanks, Jasmine — quick pricing note from AE side; Ari, copied the two clean paths so you can decide:

Option A — Short-term add-on (fast, minimal paperwork):
- Add the 6 projects as month-to-month capacity add-ons for Q1. No term change to the main renewal.
- Pricing: list + 10% (volume pricing not applied). Billed monthly; can be converted to committed uplift later.
- Pros: fast (we can start provisioning immediately), minimal procurement changes.
- Cons: higher unit price, no upfront discount.

Option B — Commit uplift (recommended if you expect steady usage):
- Increase committed capacity for 12 months starting at renewal effective date. Applies a stepped discount: 7–12% off token unit price depending on uplift band.
- We can retroactively allocate the uplift to the six projects during onboarding.
- Pros: better unit economics; single PO/renewal.
- Cons: requires procurement sign-off on adjusted commit.

If you want us to model numbers, tell us expected average tokens/day per project and preferred commit length (12 vs 24 months).

I’ve also included a sample amendment PDF (attached to Jasmine’s message). If procurement needs an alternate billing structure (e.g., monthly invoicing but single-year commitment), we can draft that into the SOW.

— Ben

Hi all — operational follow-up and timeline if Asteria picks Option B (commit uplift) or wants to start with a fast add-on (Option A).

Key provisioning & rollout (recommended 3-week cadence):
Week 1 (kickoff):
- Kickoff call (day 0) — confirm project owners and test accounts.
- We create sandbox API keys for all 6 projects within 2 business days.
- Engineering runbook share (I’ll send the onboarding checklist + sample requests).

Week 2 (staging validation):
- Each project performs smoke tests (we provide test vectors).
- We validate KV cache behavior and pre-warm model shards for projected concurrency.

Week 3 (production activation):
- Issue production API keys after smoke pass (1 day per project; we can overlap).
- Temporary increase to burst capacity allowed for cutover window (48 hours) — no charge for the first cutover if under agreed QPS.

Data we need from Asteria (small form):
- Project name + owner email (for key provisioning) — template attached (API_Key_Provisioning_Template.csv).
- Expected average QPS and peak QPS per project.
- Any IP ranges to whitelist for prod keys.

If you need a staged backfill of existing commit to include these projects, we’ll require procurement confirmation for the billable start date. I’ll also link the onboarding checklist and will take point on provisioning once we have the CSV.

Thanks — Laura
